//: The project adapter. Copy to g9.project.json in the repo of the app under test —
NOT into this tool. Everything the tool knows about your product lives here, as data,
so the extension itself stays usable on any site without being untangled from one.
//environments: A base-URL string, or the object form. The runner's --env <name> rewrites every flow URL
whose origin is ANY environment's origin onto the chosen environment's origin, resolves a
literal {{baseUrl}} in URLs, and keys the flow's known world by the environment name.
`features` and `build` are what `requires` preflight checks against for web flows
(a flow whose requires needs them on a string-form environment is SKIPPED, loudly).
//urlNormalizers: CONSUMED by the runner and replay since 3.3.0: collapse routes only your app knows are the same operation. Applied when the network signature is built AND to the stored known world at comparison, so /tasks/<guid> and /tasks/<other-guid> stop looking like two different requests.
//secretRefs: NAMES only — a value here would be a credential in a file that gets committed. CONSUMED: a recording's password fields become {{secret:<name>}} steps with a secretRef parameter; the runner resolves each from the --data file, then from G9_SECRET_<NAME> environment variables, and SKIPS a flow whose required secret has neither.
//volatile: RESERVED — not implemented: nothing reads this key yet. Use `g9 calibrate`, which finds volatile noise by running the flow twice and needs nobody to guess.
//operationAliases: RESERVED — not implemented: nothing reads this key yet. Intended for friendlier names in reports and Jira summaries.
//destructiveActions: Accessible names an exploratory run must never click. Advisory today; the state-graph explorer will enforce it.
//reportSink: RESERVED — not implemented: nothing reads this key yet. The runner writes its report files to --report (default ./g9-artifacts) regardless.
